The cast fails on those rows, and they would also duplicate txn_ids already delivered at 02:00. 1768716039000 ms is 2026-01-18 06:00:39 UTC, which matches the original row's timestamp. The fix parses epoch-ms values as UTC and keeps one row per txn_id.","decision":"fix","confidence":0.85,"pre_sql":[],"step_overrides":{"silver_transactions":"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT txn_id, customer_id, merchant_id, amount, status, ingest_ts,
         CASE WHEN regexp_matches(txn_ts, '^[0-9]+$') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS ts
  FROM raw_transactions
),
dedup AS (
  SELECT * FROM parsed
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY ingest_ts ASC) = 1
)
SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id,
       customer_id,
       CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id,
       CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount,
       ts AS txn_ts,
       CAST(ts AS DATE) AS txn_date
FROM dedup
WHERE status = 'POSTED';"}}
